$comment: Connection settings for pdfsuite. Discovered automatically by walking up from the
working directory, so `pdfsuite generate` works from anywhere in the project.
this file   HOW to reach the API — url, method, auth, headers, timeouts, and the
shape of the response. Stable, reviewed, version-controlled.
CLI flags   WHAT to process this run — --payloads, --out, --report.
An explicitly passed flag always overrides the value here.
Secrets: never commit a token. String values expand ${ENV_VAR} from the environment,
and a missing variable is a hard error rather than an empty header.
This example points at the bundled mock API (npm run mock-api).

$comment_auth: Optional. One of four shapes — each produces a header or query parameter, but
declaring it here keeps credentials out of hand-built strings (and base64-encodes
Query-string credentials are redacted from logs and from the manifest.
$comment_response: json    JSON body with a base64 string at responsePath  (default)
binary  the body IS the PDF (Content-Type: application/pdf)
base64  the whole body is a bare base64 string, no JSON wrapper

$comment_paths: Optional default paths, so a fixed output directory need not be retyped. Flags still
override. Paths that vary per run are better passed as flags.
